planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in autumn into leaf-mold-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil at the base of deciduous hardwoods; seed propagation is slow and unreliable, so division is the practical route.

directions: Finely dissected, almost thread-like leaves set this toothwort apart from the broader-leaved cutleaf and two-leaf toothworts already common in woodland gardens, giving it a distinct textural identity among its early-spring relatives. Plant divisions into rich, humus-laden soil at the base of deciduous hardwoods, matching the mixed mesophytic cove-forest conditions of its native Kentucky-Tennessee-Alabama range. Growth is notably slow to form a colony, so interplant it with faster-spreading companions like Uvularia or Asarum rather than expecting quick groundcover coverage. Foliage emerges and flowers in early-to-mid spring before canopy leaf-out, then goes fully dormant by early summer, so mark the spot to avoid disturbing the dormant rhizomes during summer garden work.
